intents.response: Hello! I am PyTutor Assistant. How can I help you learn Python today?
Python is a high-level, interpreted, and easy-to-learn programming language.
Python was created by Guido van Rossum and released in 1991.
A variable is a container used to store data values.
Data types define the type of value a variable can hold, such as int, float, string, list, etc.
A string is a sequence of characters enclosed in single or double quotes.
An integer is a whole number without decimal points.
A float is a numeric data type used for decimal numbers.
A loop is used to execute a block of code repeatedly. Python supports for loops and while loops.
A for loop is used to iterate over a sequence such as a list, tuple, string, or range.
A while loop executes as long as a given condition is True.
A function is a reusable block of code that performs a specific task.
A list is an ordered and mutable collection used to store multiple items.
A tuple is an ordered and immutable collection of items.
A set is an unordered collection of unique elements.
A dictionary stores data as key-value pairs.
Conditional statements allow a program to make decisions using if, elif, and else.
A class is a blueprint for creating objects in Object-Oriented Programming.
An object is an instance of a class.
Inheritance allows one class to acquire the properties and methods of another class.
Exception handling is used to handle runtime errors using try and except blocks.
File handling allows reading from and writing to files using functions like open().
A module is a Python file containing functions, classes, and variables that can be imported.
A package is a collection of Python modules organized in directories.
You're welcome! Happy coding.
Goodbye! Have a great day and keep learning Python.
